questions: Do line_loss_events on the s-bend and slalom fall below 1.0 per run with the wider 0.14 m track, or do they stay at 1.0?
Does steering_oscillation fall below the iteration 6 level (0.133 on the s-bend, 0.148 on the slalom), showing that turn rate was the cause of the drift?
Does progress on the oval fall with the slower turn, and does the total score exceed 70.83?
Is the first line loss still at the same bend and step as in iteration 6?

intent: Revert to the iteration 6 best geometry (70.83) and change one variable: wheel_track from 0.12 m to 0.14 m, to damp turn rate and test whether the s-bend and slalom line losses come from over-turning. Keep sensor span ±0.03 m at 12 mm footprints, y 0.05 m, mass 0.4 kg and body_length 0.16 m. Expect steering_oscillation at or below about 0.15 and line losses at or below 1.0 per run on the s-bend and slalom, with a score close to or above 70.83.
learning: Iteration 8 showed that widening the outer sensors to ±0.04 m at 0.02 m spacing (12 mm footprints) is harmful, dropping the score to 36.6 with s-bend progress at 0.04, so the sensor span is closed at ±0.03 m. Iteration 7 showed that 8 mm footprints lower the score, so 12 mm is kept. Mass 0.4 kg and body_length 0.16 m remain as the best yaw settings. Read the next race as follows: if line losses fall and oscillation drops, turn rate was the limit, and the next step is a fine adjustment of wheel_track around 0.14 to 0.16 m. If line losses and progress are unchanged, the controller, not the geometry, is limiting the robot, and the final geometry should be the iteration 6 design.
rationale: Iteration 8 is the clearest result in the history. Widening the outer sensors to x = ±0.04 m at 0.02 m spacing, with 12 mm footprints, dropped the score from 70.83 to 36.61. The s-bend collapsed from progress 0.150 to 0.040 (score 16.4), and the slalom and oval also fell. The Integrator's span branch and my own expectation both predicted a gain, so the wider span is rejected. The 0.02 m spacing leaves gaps between 12 mm footprints, and the centre signal appears to lose resolution. I therefore revert to the iteration 6 geometry, the best design at 70.83: mass 0.4 kg, body 0.16 m × 0.12 m, 12 mm footprints, sensors at x = +0.03, +0.015, 0, -0.015, -0.03 and y = 0.05 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m. The only change is wheel_track from 0.12 m to 0.14 m. Evidence across the history shows line_loss_events fixed at 1.0 per run on the s-bend and slalom, max_error at 0.061 to 0.067 m, and steering_oscillation stable at 0.13 to 0.15. The remaining untested lever with a single variable is turn rate, which the Integrator named as a damping test. Iteration 1 (narrow 0.10 m track with higher gain) did not help, so this tests slower turning rather than faster. Expected result: lower steering oscillation and possibly fewer line losses on the s-bend and slalom. Progress may fall slightly on the oval, so the score may stay close to 70.83 or rise modestly. If the score falls with line losses unchanged, the turn rate was not the limit, and I will return to the iteration 6 geometry as the base.
